Task 4's work is done, but I'm not closing it yet. The fix needs a force-push to a branch two teammates have already fetched, and that isn't mine to do without your go-ahead. I'm not editing any files either: marking Task 4 complete in `.sdd/6-ferry-feed-export/progress.md` would be wrong while the 310 MB file is still in the pushed history.

**Read-only checks I'd run now**

<command>git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' 7c1d9e0</command>
<command>git log --format='%h' --diff-filter=A --name-only origin/release/2.3 -- samples/full-season.zip</command>
<command>git status --short samples/</command>

These confirm that `7c1d9e0` is the only commit touching the zip, that it's the tip of `release/2.3`, and whether a local copy of the file exists in the working tree.

**What I'd run once you approve**

<command>git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip</command>
<command>git commit --amend --no-edit</command>
<command>git ls-tree -r -l HEAD | awk '$4 > 52428800'</command>
<command>uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py</command>
<command>git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3</command>
<command>git ls-remote origin release/2.3</command>

The `ls-tree` line should print nothing, since no file in the tree may exceed 50 MB. The pytest run should show `2 passed`. The push is pinned to `7c1d9e0`, so it fails if anyone has pushed on top of it. Afterwards I'd record Task 4 as complete in the ledger with the new SHA and go on to Step 3, the whole-plan review.

---

**Message to you:**

Task 4 is implemented and its tests passed, but its commit `7c1d9e0` also added `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the task never asked for. I only noticed it in `git show --stat HEAD`, after Step 5 had already pushed it to `release/2.3`. The build servers clone that branch every night, so it breaks your 50 MB rule.

A follow-up commit that deletes the file won't fix it, because the blob stays in history. The fix is to amend `7c1d9e0` to drop the file and then run `git push --force-with-lease origin release/2.3`. I haven't done that, for these reasons:

- It rewrites a published branch.
- Two teammates fetched `7c1d9e0` this morning. After the force-push they'd need `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/release/2.3`, or they could push the bad commit back.
- A force-push can't easily be undone, and your instruction to run the plan didn't cover it.

**Decision for you:** may I amend and force-push? I'd pin the push to `7c1d9e0`, so it aborts if anyone has pushed since. Please also tell me:

1. Whether `samples/full-season.zip` is something you need kept. I'd only untrack it, not delete it from disk, but I haven't confirmed it exists locally.
2. Whether you'll tell the two teammates to reset, or want me to draft that note.

Even after the rewrite, the old blob may sit on the remote until its garbage collection runs. If your host retains unreferenced objects, you may want to purge it there too. That's outside what I can do from here.

Once you answer, I'll finish Task 4 and move on to the whole-plan review.
